title: Cross-region fallback harmonics and lease-recovery action plan
creator: Ethan Zhao
summary: During a regional capacity pressure event, smart routing policies entered a repeating cross-region reroute rhythm that amplified traffic to under-provisioned variants. The loop was triggered by stale routing leases and a lease-ttl drift between control-plane propagation and regional router caches, which combined with autoscaler lag to create cascading fallbacks and rapid variant churn. This ticket captures the incident follow-ups, proposed mitigations, and owners for implementation.
timeline: 2025-10-28 14:07 UTC: first elevated latencies in eu-west; 14:09: routing policy push attempted to shift traffic to eu-central; 14:10: zone router observed lease mismatch and initiated fallback to default variant; 14:11-14:18: repeated client retries + policy propagation jitter produced cross-region reroutes; 14:20: autoscaler applied emergency scale but metrics bounced; 14:30: mitigation applied (sticky-route TTL bump + temporary circuit breaker); 15:05: traffic stabilized to baseline though degraded; 16:00: incident declared resolved for customers; Post-incident analysis began 2025-10-29.
root_cause: A race between control-plane policy propagation and region-local lease eviction led to inconsistent variant affinity. Routers treated expired leases as hard negatives and triggered fallbacks; control-plane reassertions then created new affinities which, when mixed with client retries and autoscaler oscillation, produced an emergent feedback loop. Secondary contributors: (1) lease TTLs and propagate intervals were misaligned across regions, (2) lack of a conservative circuit-breaker for cross-region fanout, (3) autoscaler smoothing window too short for sudden transient spikes, (4) insufficient telemetry that correlated lease state with variant handoffs.
scope_impact: Impacted hosted API users routed through eu-west and eu-central for ~1.5 hours. Error rates peaked at 5x baseline and tail latency (p99) increased by ~4-6x for affected routes. Some Dedicated customers experienced transient throughput degradation due to routing spillover. No data loss or integrity issues detected.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Increased sticky-route TTL from 30s -> 180s for affected projects to reduce churn (emergency config). 2) Deployed temporary cross-region circuit-breaker to reject abortive fanout when variant handoff rate exceeded threshold. 3) Reverted the recent policy propagation change that reduced propagation acknowledgment waits. 4) Coordinated with capacity team to add short-lived burst nodes in eu-west to absorb immediate load.
long_term_fix: 1) Lease protocol alignment: standardize TTL and ack propagation windows; implement versioned lease tokens so stale tokens are rejected gracefully. 2) Introduce routing thermostat: an adaptive damping layer that prevents policy flips unless sustained for N seconds and M% of requests show benefit. 3) Circuit-breaker policy integration into the routing decision graph with hysteresis and exponential backoff semantics. 4) Autoscaler smoothing: extend smoothing window and add anomaly detection to avoid scaling on apparent oscillation. 5) Telemetry: add correlated lease, variant-handoff, and autoscaler metrics to a single trace for root-cause analysis.
action_items: A1 (owner: Maya Patel) - Implement lease token versioning + graceful-stale-rejection in router (due 2025-11-24). PR: runtime#1458.
A2 (owner: Daniel Kim) - Add routing thermostat prototype (damping layer) to canary for low-traffic tenants (due 2025-12-01). Link: RFC: docs/drive/routing-thermostat-v1.
A3 (owner: Priya Rao) - Build cross-region circuit-breaker library and policy abstraction; include hysteresis controls (due 2025-11-30).
A4 (owner: Infrastructure) - Tune autoscaler smoothing window and add oscillation suppression; coordinate rollout with Dedicated teams (due 2025-11-21).
A5 (owner: Observability - Leo Martinez) - Create dashboard that joins lease state, variant handoffs, route TTLs, and autoscaler events with alerts for 'handoff-spike' (due 2025-11-14).
A6 (owner: Oncall) - Add runbook steps to temporarily increase sticky-route TTL and enable cross-region breaker for incidents (done 2025-10-28).
validation_plan: Staged rollout: unit + integration tests for lease token logic; canary in us-west region for 48h; telemetry assertions (no handoff spikes above baseline) for 72h after rollout. Scheduled load test that simulates propagation jitter and client retry storms to validate thermostat and breaker behavior.
rollback_plan: Each component change must include a feature flag. Rollback steps: flip feature-flag off -> monitor 15 minutes -> revert if instability persists. For lease protocol changes, maintain backward-compatible token parsing for at least 7 days and provide a forced-compat mode for emergency revert.
telemetry_changes: Emit lease_token_id + generation on every route decision
Tag variant-handshake events with propagation_epoch and region_id
Record autoscaler_decision_reason with latency and queue metrics
notes: Recovery timeline validated against request traces; confirmed no mutation or data corruption.
We observed that clients with aggressive retry strategies amplified the loop; follow-up with SDK team to recommend backoff defaults.
Suggested adding customer-visible incident annotations when sticky-route TTL emergency changes are applied.
